answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. In effect, the network makes cheating the most expensive strategy available, which is the closest thing to a Sybil-resistant design that economics allows. Consider a basalt as the anchor of the cost.
